problems.issue: Truncated HTML content and CSS response indicates potential server-side rendering or output buffering cuts.
problems.impact: Incomplete page rendering can break layout integrity and negatively impact user experience and SEO crawling.

problems.issue: Reliance on Drupal 7, an End-of-Life (EOL) Content Management System.
problems.impact: Poses severe security vulnerabilities, lacks modern performance optimizations, and complicates future feature scaling.

problems.issue: Limited visible on-page conversion elements such as direct appointment booking or prominent click-to-call buttons.
problems.impact: Reduces patient conversion rates from organic traffic looking for immediate dental services.

opportunities: Integrate a prominent online appointment scheduling widget to capture high-intent dental patients directly from the landing page.
Implement structured data (schema markup) for LocalBusiness and Dentist to significantly improve local search visibility in Cebu.
Upgrade the CMS platform to a modern framework or Drupal 10 to improve site security, mobile responsiveness, and load times.
audit.summary: The SFP Dental Clinic webpage presents a solid foundational message for patients in Cebu, but suffers from technical debt related to its legacy Drupal 7 architecture and truncated output. Strategic modernization, enhanced conversion paths (like online booking), and structured data implementation will drive higher patient acquisition and better search rankings.

outreach.subject: Quick thought on the SFP Dental Clinic site
outreach.body:
Hi there,

I was looking over cebudentalimplants.com and noticed some parts of the page layout are currently getting cut off due to a server-side rendering hiccup. Since the site is built on an older version of Drupal, it's also missing out on easy ways for patients to click-to-call or book an appointment directly from their phones.

We put together a quick, modern prototype of the SFP Dental Clinic page with a smoother mobile booking flow to see what it could look like.

Would it be useful if I sent it over?

Best,
Rahul
